question: If the length, breadth and height of a room are 15 m, 20 m, 30 m respectively, then what will be the area of four walls of the room?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The area of four walls of a room is simply its lateral surface area.

Lateral Surface Area = 2 × (length + breadth) × height

⇒ Area = 2 × (15 + 20) × 30

⇒ Area = 2 × 35 × 30 = 2100 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 2100 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the room (l) = 15 m

Breadth of the room (b) = 20 m

Height of the room (h) = 30 m

 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 
 

 

 

 
 
 l = 15 m
 b = 20 m
 h = 30 m
 
 
 Lateral Area
 = Area of 4 walls

**Formula Used:**

Area of 4 walls = Lateral Surface Area of Cuboid = 2 × (l + b) × h

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area = 2 × (15 + 20) × 30

⇒ Area = 2 × 35 × 30

⇒ Area = 70 × 30

⇒ Area = 2100 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 2100 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of Cuboid

Includes all 6 faces (4 walls + floor + ceiling) = 2(lb + bh + hl)

Volume of a Cuboid

The total space occupied by the room = l × b × h

Diagonal of a Cuboid

The length of the longest straight line or pole that can be placed inside the room = √(l² + b² + h²)
